title: S-map parameters for APSIM
author: Vogeler, Lilburne, et al.
materials: Organic matter is set up by providing the content of organic carbon (OC, %) for each layer, and a corresponding C:N ratio to define the amounts of N in each soil layer. In APSIM Classic, C:N is assumed to be constant over the soil layers. Furthermore, values for FBIOM (fraction of OM with a fast turnover rate, with a C:N of 8 commonly used), and FINert (inert fraction) need to be provided.

Through inverse modelling using APSIM with SWIM3, Vogeler, Carrick [41] found that in soils with a slowly permeable subsurface horizon the value of Ksat only had a small effect on temporal soil moisture contents and level of saturation, whereas the KDUL was much more important. Based on a sensitivity analysis, and expected ephemeral soil saturation levels from the soil morphology, Vogeler, Carrick [34] then suggested that for well-drained soils in NZ, KDUL ranges from 1 to 5 mm d−1, for moderately well drained soils from 0.1 to 0.5 mm d−1, and for poorly drained soils from 0.05 to 0.1 mm d−1. With the default value for KDUL of 0.1 mm d−1, the saturation level would be overestimated in well-drained soils and underestimated in poorly drained soils. Although, in this study the effect of poor prediction of the saturation level on denitrification and potential nitrous oxide emissions was not shown, these losses would be likewise over- and underestimated, given a sufficient amount of N in the soil. Furthermore, the choice of KDUL affected pasture yield, with both reduced yield (up to 13%) and increased yield (up to 8%), depending on the soil and climatic condition.

steps.title: Select soil sibling and model
steps.instruction: Choose the appropriate S‑map sibling for the site (use the first‑listed sibling if no field data are available) and decide whether to use the SoilWater or SWIM3 water‑balance model.

substeps.instruction: Open S‑map (smap.landcareresearch.co.nz) and locate the map polygon of interest.
Record the sibling name (four‑ or five‑character abbreviation) and its functional horizons.
Note the desired water model (SoilWater or SWIM3) for the APSIM simulation.

steps.title: Create or copy a soil in APSIM
steps.instruction: In APSIM, start from an existing soil (e.g., from the APSoil database) and save it under a new name; do not create a soil from scratch unless preferred.

substeps.instruction: Open APSIM and load a soil that is similar to the selected sibling.
Use the ‘Save As’ function to give the copy a new name (e.g., MySite_Soil).
All subsequent parameter entry will be performed on this copy.

steps.title: Enter basic soil descriptors
steps.instruction: Fill the Base Soil Node with location, name, texture and sibling information.

substeps.instruction: Enter geographic coordinates (latitude, longitude).
Enter the soil name (e.g., MySite_Soil).
Enter the soil texture (sand‑silt‑clay percentages).
Enter the S‑map sibling name.

steps.title: Define layer structure
steps.instruction: Create soil layers that follow the functional horizon boundaries and the thickness rules for the chosen water model.

substeps.instruction: For SoilWater: set maximum top‑layer thickness to 200 mm and all other layers to ≤600 mm. If a functional horizon exceeds 200 mm (top) or 600 mm (others), split it evenly; if it exceeds 900 mm, split into three equal layers.
For SWIM3: split the top functional horizon into layers of 10, 20, 30, 40 mm in that order; any remainder is divided into 100 mm increments (e.g., an 80 mm horizon becomes 10 + 20 + 30 + 20 mm).
Below the top horizon, add one layer per functional horizon; if a horizon is >150 mm, split it into equal layers between 75 mm and 150 mm.
For the bottom functional horizon (usually >1 m), add two 50 mm layers and a final 20 mm layer.
Assume a zero matric‑potential gradient below the bottom boundary (or optionally add a fluctuating water table or subsurface drains).

steps.title: Enter particle size distribution
steps.instruction: Input sand, silt and clay percentages, adjusting the sand‑silt boundary from 0.06 mm (NZ) to 0.05 mm (APSIM) if needed.

steps.title: Enter rock fragment content
steps.instruction: Record the percentage of coarse fragments (≥ 2.0 mm) for each functional horizon and apply the rock‑adjustment to hydraulic parameters later.

steps.title: Calculate bulk density
steps.instruction: Compute bulk density (BD) for each horizon using total porosity (TP) and particle density (PD) according to soil order, then adjust for rocks.

substeps.instruction: Select PD based on soil order:
‑ Orders M and L → PD = 2.45 g cm⁻³
‑ Orders G, Z and N → PD = 2.53 g cm⁻³
‑ All other orders (R, P, B, A, W, E, S, X) → PD = 2.65 g cm⁻³
Compute BDmatrix = PD × (1 – TP).
If the horizon contains > 80 % sand and 0 % (text appears truncated – retain as‑is).
Adjust for rocks: BDadj = BDmatrix × (1 – frocks) + frocks × BDrocks, where frocks is the rock‑fragment fraction.

steps.title: Enter soil chemical properties
steps.instruction: Provide pH, CEC and other chemical parameters in the appropriate node (Analysis & Initial N for Classic, Chemical for Next Generation).

substeps.instruction: Set pH to a neutral value between 6.0 and 7.0 (or use measured/predicted values).
Calculate CEC using CEC = 2.25 fOC + 0.267 fC + 0.067 fS, where fOC, fC and fS are the organic‑carbon, clay and silt fractions (expressed as fractions, not percentages).

steps.title: Enter water‑retention parameters
steps.instruction: For each layer, input LL15, DUL, SAT and AirDry values derived from S‑map and apply the required adjustments.

substeps.instruction: Copy LL15, DUL and SAT directly from the S‑map factsheet (these are volumetric water contents, cm³ cm⁻³).
Compute AirDry:
‑ If horizon depth > 300 mm → AirDry = 0.5 × LL15
‑ If horizon depth ≤ 300 mm → AirDry = LL15
‑ If a horizon straddles 300 mm, use a weighted mean of the two adjacent AirDry values.
Compute SAT as 0.93 × TP (total porosity) and adjust TP for rock fraction.
If SAT < DUL, replace SAT with SAT = DUL + 0.75 × (TP – DUL) for DUL ≥ 0.93 TP.

steps.title: Enter saturated hydraulic conductivity
steps.instruction: Provide KS (fhKsat) for each horizon, converting units from mm h⁻¹ to mm d⁻¹.

substeps.instruction: Read KS (fhKsat) from the S‑map supplementary Table S1 (units: mm h⁻¹).
Convert: KS_mm_d = KS_mm_h × 24.
For SoilWater the KS entry is optional; if omitted, infiltration is limited only by SAT and excess water runs off or drains.

steps.title: Enter soil‑plant specific parameters
steps.instruction: Provide LL, KL and XF for each layer up to the crop‑specific maximum rooting depth (RZmax).

substeps.instruction: Set LL = LL15 for the layer (unless a different value is justified).
Obtain crop‑specific KL0, RZmax, PRresp and PRthresh from Table 1 (e.g., Barley: KL0 = 0.061 mm mm⁻¹ d⁻¹, RZmax = 1500 mm, PRresp = 1.20, PRthresh = 0.1).
Compute depth factor f(z):
‑ If mean depth z¯ ≤ 300 mm → f(z) = 1
Calculate crop potential CP = KL0 × f(z).
Obtain KLfh for the functional horizon from Supplementary Table S1 and compute KL = CP × KLfh.
Compute XF:
‑ If PRresist < PRthresh → XF = 1
‑ Otherwise XF = PRresist / PRthresh, where PRresist = XFfh × 5 (XFfh from Supplementary Table S1).
Enter these three values (LL, KL, XF) in the soil node for each layer up to RZmax; set them to zero below RZmax.

steps.title: Enter organic‑matter pools
steps.instruction: Specify organic‑carbon content and the fast‑turnover (FBIOM) and inert (FINert) fractions for each layer based on previous land use.

substeps.instruction: Read OC (%) for each horizon from S‑map.
Determine previous land use (Pasture or Crop).
For Pasture:
For Crop:
Enter OC, FBIOM and FINert in the SoilOrganicMatter node (Classic) or Organic node (Next Generation).
Note: Fresh organic material (FOM) parameters are not covered in this protocol.

steps.title: Enter model‑specific parameters
steps.instruction: Provide SWCON for SoilWater or KDUL for SWIM3 and set solute‑adsorption parameters.

substeps.instruction: For SoilWater:
‑ Retrieve SWCON for each functional horizon from Supplementary Table S1 and enter it in the SoilWater node.
‑ SWCON represents the proportion of water above DUL that drains per day.
For SWIM3:
‑ Choose a KDUL value based on drainage class:
• Well‑drained soils: 1 – 5 mm d⁻¹
• Moderately well‑drained: 0.1 – 0.5 mm d⁻¹
• Poorly drained: 0.05 – 0.1 mm d⁻¹
‑ Enter the selected KDUL (single value for the whole profile) in the SWIM3 node.
Enter SoluteParameters for NH₄⁺:
‑ Compute k (Exco) = 30.84 – 1.263 × CEC + 1.235 × fclay
‑ Compute n (Fip) = 0.46 + 0.013 × CEC – 0.006 × fclay
‑ Enter k and n in the SoluteParameters child node (other solutes may use k = 0, n = 1).

steps.title: Save and verify soil definition
steps.instruction: Save the completed soil definition and optionally run a short test simulation to confirm that all parameters are accepted.

substeps.instruction: Click ‘Save’ in APSIM.
Run a quick simulation (e.g., a single day with no crops) to check for errors.
If errors appear, revisit the relevant step and correct the values.

description: APSIM is a modelling framework designed and maintained by the APSIM Initiative. A detailed description of the various models within the APSIM framework can be found on the website (www.apsim.info). An abridged description of the models used to simulate soil processes in APSIM is provided in [11]. The paper also lists and describes the basic soil inputs (including physical and chemical characteristics), and how to enter specific parameters in the interface, based on measurements or pedotransfer functions. Currently there are two versions of APSIM available: APSIM Classic is several decades old, with dated infrastructure, and is gradually being recoded as APSIM Next Generation, which retains much of the earlier functionality but with a modern and more maintainable code base. Both versions contain the same soil models and mostly use the same soil parameters, but the user interface varies somewhat. For modelling soil water movement and solute transport, two different approaches are available for most modelling purposes: SoilWater (also called SoilWat; [12]) and SWIM3 [13]). (SWIM2 is only recommended for very experienced APSIM users and its parameterisation is not described here.) SoilWater is based on the tipping bucket approach, and SWIM3 on the Richards’ equation and the convection dispersion equation. These models differ in the approach and level of complexity used to describe the relevant processes. They have many parameters in common but others that differ, as described below. Within the APSIM interface, a simulation is a collection of nodes, with the soil node being one of the fundamental components of an APSIM simulation. The soil node is itself a container, with several further child nodes, which comprise entry points for general soil parameterisation (layer structure, physical and chemical properties, etc.), as well as for setting up model-specific parameters (SoilWater, SoilTemperature).
